consequence: Both policies stay legacy. The FAIL is kept; a further attempt is a new registered version.
analysis: Start-up: C2 (upstream-like: first+last piece urgent, 0 / 2000+1000*d ms) improves time-to-start beyond noise in both series in 5 of 6 key cells and is not worse at 1 MiB pieces: fast 4 MiB 6.8 -> 4.8 s, fast 16 MiB 13.2 -> 9.1 s, thin 1 MiB 6.35 -> 5.47 s, thin 4 MiB 9.6 -> 6.7 s, thin 16 MiB 14.5 -> 11.25 s; also at 8 and 60 Mbit/s on fast. C1 (graded) repeats its v1 regression at 1 MiB pieces (TTFB +0.3-0.4 s).

Blocking regression for both candidates: seek resume with 16 MiB pieces, thin 3.46 -> 6.8-8.2 s (C2) / 8.5-9.0 s (C1), fast +0.4-1.5 s. Legacy (C0) fetches the first post-seek 16 MiB piece in ~3.4 s at 5 MB/s, i.e. at the line-rate minimum; the candidates take about twice as long, so bandwidth is shared with something else.
Not the priority leak: C2 downloads less unused data than C0 (thin/16MiB 55 vs 88 MB).

Working hypothesis (static, unmeasured): at a seek the previous stream may still wait for an undownloaded piece and keep it urgent (deadline 0) until it notices the disconnect; with the candidates' looser window deadlines that piece is more often incomplete at seek time. To be measured before any v3.
Other regressions are at noise level (e.g. fast/16MiB/8Mbit TTFB +0.056 s with J 0.05 s) or in the noisy mixed guard cells.
Tracebacks (raw logs not kept): C0 4, C1 2, C2 8 in 120 runs each, also present in C0: the same rare fork defect as in pb0-v2, not candidate-specific; diagnosis pending.
next: Diagnose the seek slowdown (stream lifetime and piece deadlines around a seek) and the traceback source with instrumented diagnostic runs; only then a gsp02-v3 candidate.
